newsitem.title: USA: CME feeder cattle tumble to lower close on funds.
newsitem.headline: CME feeder cattle tumble to lower close on funds.

text.p: Massive fund liquidation and chart-based sell stops pushed CME feeder cattle down for sharp losses by the close, traders said. Live cattle futures also posted closing losses on ideas the next move in cash markets will be lower.
Feeder cattle ended 1.200 to 0.050 cents per lb lower with August off most at 77.000 cents. Live cattle ended 0.350 to 0.075 cent a lb lower with August off 0.350 at 64.975 cents.

Long fund liquidation and plentiful sell stops in the feeder pit under 78.000 cents, basis August, pushed feeders lower. Charts looked toppy after failing to post new contract highs earlier in the week, traders said.

Feeders failed to post new highs despite strong buying interest early this week and futures have eased since. Adding to pressure was the premium futures hold to cash feeder cattle prices and expected reduced demand for feeders. Fed cattle prices are expected to start a seasonal downtrend soon and feedlots already have plenty of cattle, they said.

"At $64 (fed cattle) it puts most breakevens for the feedlot operators right at the zero or a little bit in the red so you have to expect them to start paying less for feeders," said Dean Witter analyst, Dale Benson.
"They are pretty full on (fed) cattle so there is no reason not to" pay less for feeders, Benson said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.16 at $77.76 per cwt.
Cargill Investor Services actively sold August while buying next year contracts. LFG and ING also sold August. Lind-Waldock sold September in late trade, pit sources said.

Live cattle slipped as ideas the next move in cash markets will be lower, weighed on futures. Despite recent strength in cash fed cattle and boxed beef prices and demands for deliveries, cash beef prices were seen slipping after retailers finish buying for the Independence Day holiday, which should be any day now, traders said.
Packers will have plenty of cattle to choose from based on large on-feed supplies available the next couple of months, they added.
USDA last week reported that the number of cattle on feed in large feedlots in the seven key states was 13 percent above a year ago.
ABN Amro-Chicogo Corp sold June while R.J. O'Brien bought August and sold June. Lind-Waldock bought August while Cargill and mixed commission house sold, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses bought August 60 and 61 puts and sold October 68 calls, pit sources added.

Trade in boneless beef and boneless beef trimings increased after a slow start, traders said. Profit-taking and speculative selling weighed on boneless beef but scattered support was still evident on expected strength going into the holiday period. Trimmings followed action in live cattle despite commercial buying at times. More trimmings are expected to be offered before the holiday, traders said.
Boneless closed 0.20 cent per lb lower to 0.20 higher with August off most at 94.00. Trimmings ended 0.100 lower to 0.20 higher with August off 0.10 at 42.40 cents.
